pdf_title: A hybrid data-level ensemble to enable learning from highly imbalanced dataset
srcdet: 28 datasets taken from the KEEL repository; 14 taken from the LibSVM website (vowel0, german, svmguide3, breast-cancer, diabetes, svmguide1, gisette, australian, a1a, mushrooms, phishing, skinnonskin, cod, ijcnn), from which the authors randomly removed minority instances to raise IR. Source column of Table 1 gives the repository per dataset.
crit: KEEL is 'a repository containing imbalanced datasets that have been constantly used as benchmark datasets in this field'; because 'the highest IR in KEEL is approximately 100', 14 LibSVM datasets were made highly imbalanced 'to evaluate the proposed HD-Ensemble for extreme case', and a pre-experiment confirmed 'significantly different classification rates across different classes' on these 14.
imbalance_creation: KEEL datasets used as distributed (paper describes no modification). For the 14 LibSVM datasets the authors 'randomly removed some minority instances from each dataset' so all have IR > 9 and 4 have IR > 400; which class is minority for each LibSVM dataset is not stated.
duplicates_or_filtering: Experiment 2 only: cod, gisette and skinnonskin were removed for computational feasibility. No duplicate handling stated.
split_protocol: 5-fold stratified cross validation repeated 10 times (5 x 10 CV)
ir_definition: the ratio of majority instances to minority instances

evidence.quote: In this study, the concerns are the binary classification tasks, in which there is a majority (negative) class with significant more instances, and a minority (positive) class with much less instances.

42 highly imbalanced binary datasets were employed as the benchmark datasets. 28 of them were extracted from KEEL [1], which is a repository containing imbalanced datasets that have been constantly used as benchmark datasets in this field.
However, the highest IR in KEEL is approximately 100. To evaluate the proposed HD-Ensemble for extreme case, we manually created 14 highly imbalanced datasets.

Specifically, 14 datasets were extracted from the LibSVM website,1 and we randomly removed some minority instances from each dataset. In this way, all 14 datasets exhibited high imbalance ratio (IR > 9) and 4 of them exhibited an extremely high imbalance ratio (IR > 400).
we conducted a pre-experiment on these 14 datasets with standard learning algorithms, and significantly different classification rates across different classes were detected on all the datasets.
All the 42 datasets adopted in our experiments have been uploaded to GitHub,2 and the source code of HD-Ensemble will be uploaded to the same repository once this paper has been published.
